name: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
description: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command (-EncodedCommand or any abbreviation). Attackers encode commands to hide them from command-line logging and simple keyword searches.
note:
## Triage

1. Expand the alert. Read `process.command_line` and decode the base64 after the -e / -EncodedCommand flag (CyberChef: "From Base64" then "Decode text: UTF-16LE").
2. Check `process.parent.name`. Unusual parents (wmiprvse.exe, Office apps, browsers, script hosts) raise severity.
3. If `process.name` is not powershell.exe/pwsh.exe, PowerShell was renamed. Treat as high priority.
4. Search Discover for event.code 4104 on the same host and time to see the decoded script PowerShell actually ran.
5. Check `user.name` and whether this user/host normally runs automation.

## Notes

- Matches every abbreviation of -EncodedCommand with any leading dash character (-, /, en dash, em dash).
- Sysmon only: one alert per process. Coverage depends on Sysmon; the "Sysmon silent - ws01" rule alerts if Sysmon data stops.
- Renamed PowerShell is detected via process.pe.original_file_name (Sysmon).

## Known false positives

- Some management/deployment tools launch PowerShell with -EncodedCommand. Validate the parent process and decoded content before closing.

## Validation

Atomic Red Team T1059.001 tests 17 and 15 (EnDash variation), plus a renamed copy of powershell.exe. Verified 2026-10-04.
false_positives: Some management and deployment tools launch PowerShell with -EncodedCommand.
query: process where event.type == "start" and (process.name : ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe") or ?process.pe.original_file_name : ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")) and process.args : ("?e", "?ec", "?en", "?enc", "?enco", "?encod", "?encode", "?encoded", "?encodedc", "?encodedco", "?encodedcom", "?encodedcomm", "?encodedcomma", "?encodedcomman", "?encodedcommand")
